REMEDIATION OF AQUEOUS SOLUTIONS CONTAMINATED BY DIVALENT COBALT CATIONS USING CERATOPHYLLUM DEMERSUM PLANT AS A NON-CONVENTIONAL ADSORBENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Batool Majid Saeed, Zahraa Ahmed Mahdi, Luma Saleem Raheem, Mohammed Nsaif Abbas
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

ABSTRACT

The concept of zero residue level is primarily associated with the attempt to utilize waste in beneficial ways to treat polluted environments. From this perspective, exploiting plants that cause environmental problems to treat water contamination is a fundamental pillar of the zero-residue level concept, given that they grow and thrive in water. The present research is concerned with the study of the use of the Ceratophyllum demersum plant, which is widespread in most Iraqi water bodies, as a valueless adsorption medium for treating water contaminated with toxic heavy metals. The feasibility of this plant for recovering divalent cobalt cations from simulated solutions contaminated with hazardous cobalt was investigated in a batch adsorption unit under different operating conditions. The remediation ability was investigated at various ranges of temperature, contact time, Ceratophyllum demersum dosage, pH, agitation speed, and initial concentration of cobalt. The obtained results showed that the adsorption efficiency was inversely proportional to the initial concentration of cobalt ions, and directly proportional to the remaining variables. The increasing of acidity related with increasing the recovery percentage of cobalt ion to a certain point, after which it began to decrease. The maximum cobalt ion removal efficiency and adsorption capacity of the adsorbent were 93.2% and 0.07 mg/g, respectively. The results also exhibited that the Langmuir model was the best to describe the isothermal adsorption behavior, while the pseudo-second-order model and the intra-particle diffusion model were the closest to describing the adsorption kinetically, due to the high values of the correlation coefficient. Thermodynamically, the adsorption was chemical, positive enthalpy and entropy, and spontaneous in the temperature range studied. Morphological examinations indicated that the adsorbent possesses a variety of functional groups responsible for the high adsorption efficiency, according to FTIR analysis, and that 95% of the surface area was consumed during treatment. FESEM images, XRD, and XRF analyses revealed that Ceratophyllum demersum suffered from significant changes in its surface structure due to the accumulation of cobalt ions.
